title: Set 104

sentences.ko: 매주 사는 똑같은 네 가지만 사러 갔는데 61달러가 나왔어. 영수증을 들고 서서 뭐가 두 번 찍혔나 하고 한참 들여다봤지. 뒤에 서 있던 사람도 눈치챘는지 내가 입을 떼기도 전에 계란값 얘기를 하더라. 비싼 걸 사는 것도 아닌데, 그게 제일 답답해. 갈 때마다 그냥 더 나와.
sentences.text: I went in for the same four things I get every week and it came to sixty one dollars, so I stood there staring at the receipt like they'd rung something up twice. And the guy behind me could tell, because he said something about the eggs before I even opened my mouth. I'm not buying anything fancy, that's the part that gets me. It's just more every single time.

alts.text: Same four things I grab every week, and it came out to sixty one dollars. I just stood there staring at the receipt like they'd scanned something twice. The guy behind me could tell, too, cause he said something about the eggs before I even opened my mouth. I'm not buying fancy stuff, that's the part that gets me. It's just more every single time.

I went in for the same four items I purchase every week, and the total came to sixty one dollars. I stood there studying the receipt, wondering whether something had been rung up twice. The gentleman behind me must have noticed, because he remarked on the eggs before I had said a word. I am not buying anything extravagant, and that is what bothers me. It is simply more every single time.

sentences.note: **that's the part that gets me** 는 여러 가지 중에 특히 그 점이 마음에 걸린다고 할 때 씁니다. **rung up** 은 계산대에서 물건값이 찍혔다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 주말 내내 집 밖으로 한 발짝도 안 나갔는데 내일 또 그래도 좋아. 창문 열어 놓고, 토요일에 영화 반 보고 일요일에 나머지 반 보고, 그게 다였어. 평소 같으면 일요일 오후쯤엔 좀이 쑤시는데 이번엔 그렇지가 않더라. 내가 생각한 것보다 이게 더 필요했나 보다 싶어.
sentences.text: I didn't leave the apartment once all weekend and I'd do it again tomorrow. I had the windows open, I watched half a movie Saturday and the other half Sunday, and that was about it. Usually I'm climbing the walls by Sunday afternoon, but this time I just wasn't, so I'm taking that as a sign I needed it more than I thought.

alts.text: Didn't step out of the apartment once all weekend and I'd do it again tomorrow. Windows open, half a movie Saturday, the other half Sunday, that was it. Normally I'm going stir crazy by Sunday afternoon, but this time I just wasn't, so I figure I needed it more than I thought.

I did not leave the apartment once all weekend, and I would gladly do the same tomorrow. I kept the windows open, I watched half of a film on Saturday and the other half on Sunday, and that was the extent of it. I am usually restless by Sunday afternoon, but on this occasion I was not, so I am taking that as a sign that I needed it more than I realized.

sentences.note: **climbing the walls** 와 **going stir crazy** 는 둘 다 갇혀 있어서 좀이 쑤신다는 뜻입니다. **I'm taking that as a sign** 은 그걸 그런 뜻으로 받아들인다고 할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 금요일에 배송 완료라고 떠 있는데 물건이 없어. 그래서 복도를 오르락내리락하면서 집집마다 문을 두드리고 다녔어, 무슨 미친 사람처럼. 겨우 전화가 연결됐더니 영업일로 사흘은 기다려 보라는 거야. 배송 완료라고 뜬 뒤에 오는 경우도 있다나. 일요일이 여동생 생일인데, 그냥 다시 사야 하나 고민이야.
sentences.text: They marked it delivered on Friday and it's not here, so I've been up and down the hall knocking on doors like some kind of lunatic. And when I finally got somebody on the phone she told me to give it three business days, because apparently it sometimes shows up after they say it's delivered. It's my sister's birthday on Sunday, so now I have to decide if I just go buy it again.

alts.text: It says delivered Friday and it's just not here, so I've been up and down the hall knocking on doors like a crazy person. Then I finally get somebody on the phone and she tells me to give it three business days, cause apparently it turns up sometimes after they say it's delivered. My sister's birthday is Sunday, so now I gotta decide if I just go buy it again.

It was marked delivered on Friday and it is not here, so I have been going up and down the hall knocking on doors. When I finally reached someone by telephone, she advised me to allow three business days, as packages apparently do arrive at times after they are marked delivered. It is my sister's birthday on Sunday, so I now have to decide whether to simply purchase it again.

sentences.note: **give it three business days** 는 영업일 기준으로 사흘은 더 기다려 보라는 말입니다. **turns up** 은 없던 물건이 불쑥 나타나는 것입니다.

sentences.ko: 오시기 전에 소파 얘기부터 할게요. 왼쪽 쿠션에 고양이가 긁어 놓은 자국이 있어요. 그 쿠션을 뒤집으면 진짜 티도 안 나는데, 없는 척하고 싶지는 않아서요. 뼈대는 튼튼하고 삐걱거리지도 않아요. 그게 걸리시면 지금 말씀해 주세요, 그럼 다시 올려놓을게요.
sentences.text: Before you drive over I should tell you about the couch, there's a spot on the left cushion where my cat clawed it. You can flip that cushion over and you'd honestly never know, but I'm not going to pretend it isn't there. The frame's solid, it doesn't creak or anything. So if that's a deal breaker just say so now and I'll put it back up.

alts.text: Quick heads up about the couch before you drive over, there's a spot on the left cushion where my cat clawed it. You can flip that cushion and you'd honestly never know, but I'm not gonna act like it isn't there. Frame's solid, doesn't creak or anything. So if that's a deal breaker just say so now and I'll put it back up.

Before you drive over, I should tell you about the couch. There is a spot on the left cushion where my cat clawed it. You can turn that cushion over and you would honestly never know, but I do not want to pretend that it is not there. The frame is solid and it does not creak at all. If that is a deal breaker, please say so now and I will list it again.

sentences.note: **deal breaker** 는 그것 하나 때문에 거래를 접게 되는 결정적인 문제입니다. **heads up** 은 미리 해 주는 귀띔이고, **put it back up** 은 판매 글을 다시 올린다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 중고로 물건 팔면서 상태 솔직히 말하기

sentences.ko: 다들 좋다고 하는 무선 청소기를 샀는데, 정말이지 쓰던 게 멀쩡했어. 이건 거실 반쯤 하다가 꺼져. 그래서 청소하다 말고 서서 충전하고 있어, 이러려고 산 게 아닌데. 반품도 못 해, 오는 날 바로 상자를 접어서 버렸거든. 아내는 그 얘기를 한마디도 안 꺼내. 그냥 쓰던 걸 계속 써.
sentences.text: I bought the cordless vacuum that everybody swears by, and I'm telling you, the old one was fine. This one dies halfway through the living room, so I'm standing there charging it in the middle of cleaning, which is not what I signed up for. And I can't send it back because I broke the box down the same day it came. My wife hasn't said one word about it. She just keeps using the old one.

alts.text: I got the cordless vacuum everybody swears by, and I'm telling you, the old one was fine. This thing dies halfway through the living room, so there I am charging it in the middle of cleaning, which is not what I signed up for. And I can't send it back cause I broke the box down the same day it came. My wife hasn't said one word about it. She just keeps using the old one.

I purchased the cordless vacuum that everyone swears by, and I must say the old one was fine. This one dies halfway through the living room, so I find myself charging it in the middle of cleaning, which is not what I signed up for. I cannot send it back, as I broke the box down the same day it arrived. My wife has not said one word about it. She simply continues to use the old one.

sentences.note: **everybody swears by** 는 다들 써 보고 좋다고 하는 것입니다. **not what I signed up for** 는 내가 기대한 건 이게 아니었다는 뜻이고, **broke the box down** 은 상자를 납작하게 접어 버렸다는 말입니다.

reviewed: 1번 casual 의 "it rang up to sixty one dollars" 는 원어민이 잘 안 쓰는 말이라 "it came out to sixty one dollars" 로 고쳤습니다 (rung up 은 text 와 formal 에 그대로 남아 있어 note 는 그대로 둡니다).
2번 casual 이 뒷부분을 text 와 글자까지 똑같이 쓰고 있어서, 끝을 "so I figure I needed it more than I thought" 로 줄이고 "and that was about it" 도 "that was it" 으로 짧게 했습니다 — 캐주얼은 더 짧고 축약된 말이어야 합니다.
